title: Normalized finite open external-tensor comparison
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F_{p^a}}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$. Use a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] with its specified canonical exchange and projection transformations [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf]. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all morphisms are separated of finite type. Integral pullbacks and tensors are completed; field operations use rationalization and common finite stages. Fix finite coefficients $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. Let $\bar X\to B$, $\bar Y\to B$ be morphisms and let $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $k:Y\hookrightarrow\bar Y$ be open immersions. Put $\bar T=\bar X\times_B\bar Y$, $T=X\times_BY$, and $u=j\times_Bk:T\hookrightarrow\bar T$, with projections $\bar p,\bar q$ on $\bar T$ and $p,q$ on $T$. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, set $D=Lp^*K\otimes^LLq^*L$. The canonical open base-change maps and open projection transformations determine a natural isomorphism
$$e_{j,k}:L\bar p^*j_!K\otimes^LL\bar q^*k_!L\xrightarrow{\sim}u_!D$$
whose restriction along $u$ is the identity of $D$. More precisely, factor $u=j_1k_1$ through $X\times_B\bar Y$. Open base change of $j$, projection formula for $j_1$, open base change of $k$, and projection formula for $k_1$ (using the signed symmetry to put its extension factor first), followed by $j_{1!}k_{1!}\cong u_!$, give this isomorphism. The construction using the opposite factorization through $\bar X\times_BY$ gives the same map. Under a swap of factors, the maps $e_{j,k}$ intertwine the signed external tensor symmetries. For any third open immersion $l:W\hookrightarrow\bar W$ over $B$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$, the two composites built from $e$ on $\bar X\times_B\bar Y\times_B\bar W$ agree after the canonical associators and normalized composition identifications of extension by zero. Both restrict to the identity on $K\boxtimes L\boxtimes M$, where $\boxtimes$ means tensor of the projection pullbacks.

proof.text: Work with $A=A_{E,n}$ on the ordinary unbounded pro-etale derived categories. For composable opens $w,v$, the composite adjunction and the unique unit-preserving left-adjoint comparison give $c_{v,w}:v_!w_!\cong(vw)_!$. Its restriction is the identity: its defining unit equation becomes this assertion after the open units are inverted. For three opens the two composites carry the same pasted unit to the composite unit, hence coincide by uniqueness. These are the composition identifications in the statement.

Apply [lem-pur-finite-open-product-swap] with $\bar Z=\bar Y$, $Z=Y$, the given structure maps to $B$, $M=K$ and $N=L$. Its hypotheses hold (same $A_{E,n}$ and $k$, separated finite-type schemes and morphisms, arbitrary objects). Its $C,P,r,t,p,q,u,E,D$ are $\bar T,T,\bar p,\bar q,p,q,u$, the source of $e_{j,k}$ and $D$ here, and its $e_{j,k}$ is the composite of the statement through $X\times_B\bar Y$: base change of $j$, projection map for $j_1$, base change of $k$, projection map for $k_1$ after the signed symmetry, then the compositor. It is an isomorphism with $u^*e_{j,k}=1_D$, and it equals $e^{\mathrm{op}}_{j,k}$ built through $\bar X\times_BY$. Its $\beta,\gamma$ are those of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], which at constant finite coefficients are the canonical exchange and projection maps. Its compositor [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] is the identity on sections over the small open, as are the section-normalized units; so it carries the composite unit to the unit and is $c_{j_1,k_1}$ of step 1 by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. Naturality in $K,L$: every arrow is natural.

proof.text: The swap clause of [lem-pur-finite-open-product-swap], for the same data, gives $e_{j,k}=u_!(\sigma_{Lq^*L,Lp^*K})\circ\widetilde e_{k,j}\circ\sigma_{L\bar p^*j_!K,L\bar q^*k_!L}$, where $\widetilde e_{k,j}$ is $e_{k,j}$ on $\bar Y\times_B\bar X$ transported by the swap and normalized open base change. Compose with $u_!(\sigma_{Lp^*K,Lq^*L})$ and use $\sigma_{N,M}\circ\sigma_{M,N}=1$ for the signed symmetry: $u_!(\sigma)\circ e_{j,k}=\widetilde e_{k,j}\circ\sigma$. So the maps $e$ intertwine the signed symmetries; the target $u_!(Lq^*L\otimes^LLp^*K)$ is $u_!\tau^*(L\boxtimes K)$ by pullback composition along the swap $\tau$.

proof.text: For the third open $l$ and $M$, $\bar X\times_B\bar Y$ and $\bar Y\times_B\bar W$ are separated of finite type. Step 2 at the pairs $(j,k)$ on $(K,L)$, $(k,l)$ on $(L,M)$, $(j\times_Bk,l)$ on $(K\boxtimes L,M)$ and $(j,k\times_Bl)$ on $(K,L\boxtimes M)$ gives isomorphisms with identity restriction. Its objects are arbitrary, so no constructibility of $K\boxtimes L$ is used. These are the four normalized maps in the hypothesis of [lem-sf-open-normalized-product-coherence-criterion] with $A=A_{E,n}$, and its $F,G$ are the two composites of the statement, with the canonical associators and the composition identifications of step 1. It gives $v^*F=v^*G=1_{K\boxtimes L\boxtimes M}$ and $F=G$, which is the final clause.
